card.name: Jarabe Tapatío
card.era: Jalisco 19th century · Mexican national dance since 1924
card.tagline: The Mexican Hat Dance — Jalisco's courtship dance where the woman dances upon the man's discarded sombrero, declared the national dance in 1924.
card.profile: The Jarabe Tapatío — the Mexican Hat Dance — is the national dance of Mexico, codified in the early 19th century by the dancers of Jalisco state and proclaimed national heritage by the Mexican Ministry of Public Education in 1924. The dance is a courtship narrative in eight to twelve sequenced sections, performed by a couple in traditional charro (man) and china poblana (woman) costume. The climactic moment comes when the man throws his wide-brimmed sombrero to the floor and the woman, accepting his suit, dances atop it. The accompanying mariachi music — most famously the El Jarabe Tapatío composition — is recognised globally as the sound of Mexico.
card.insight: The Jarabe Tapatío was officially declared Mexico's national dance in 1924 by the Mexican Ministry of Public Education during the post-revolutionary cultural codification programme. The dance's signature climactic moment — when the woman dances on the man's discarded sombrero — became the visual emblem of Mexican identity worldwide, performed at every major Mexican state event from presidential inaugurations to Día de la Independencia and at the openings of Mexican cultural centres across the global Mexican diaspora.
